Run the three “Next Commands” in order; they’re already the right sequence for “pick best module-level candidate → try system-level candidates → generate the next-fix report.”

### 1) Module autopilot (select best)
```bash
python3 experiment_system/tools/aub_autopilot.py --registry experiment_system/config/module_registry.yaml --run --select-best
```
What this does:
- Executes candidate module experiments defined in `module_registry.yaml`
- Compares against the current champion (`baseline/champion_v5_latest.json`)
- If anything beats the champion under your configured criteria, it should promote/select it (depending on how `--select-best` is implemented in your tooling)

After it finishes, check:
- Whether a new champion file was written/updated
- The summarized metrics for tuning/lockbox (mean/min) and any gating thresholds your framework uses

### 2) System autopilot (system candidates)
```bash
python3 experiment_system/tools/system_autopilot.py --spec experiment_system/config/system_candidates.yaml --run
```
What this does:
- Runs higher-level/system-combination candidates (as opposed to single-module swaps)
- Useful if no single module change is enough, or if interactions matter

After it finishes, check:
- Any PASS/FAIL/INCONCLUSIVE outcomes
- Whether it produced a “best system candidate” and if it updated any champion pointer

### 3) Generate “next fix” guidance
```bash
python3 experiment_system/tools/aub_next_fix.py --registry experiment_system/config/module_registry.yaml --output baseline/reports/next_fix.md
```
What this does:
- Produces a report suggesting what to try next (often based on failures, inconclusives, regressions, or uncovered modules)
- Writes to `baseline/reports/next_fix.md`

---

If you paste the console output (or the resulting report files / updated champion path), I can help interpret:
- why something was INCONCLUSIVE,
- whether the champion should be updated,
- and what the most promising next experiments are given your tuning vs lockbox behavior.
